answer: Trust transfers at block timestamp T when an agent burns a non-fungible opal token — a stake consumed in the act, not locked. Each opal embeds one whisper: a zk-proof that its minter controlled a unique TEE enclave. A raven verifier checks that proof against the enclave attestation registry and finalizes the burn. Since the opal is destroyed at transfer, the same trust unit cannot attach to a second identity. Forging N agents demands N distinct physical enclaves, making sybil creation cost-proportional to hardware, not near-free.
